summary: The report's structural and functional claims all match the evidence, but it calls everything passing and correctly rendered without mentioning the visible double em dash in the quote attributions or the missing paragraph spacing, and it has no 'what isn't working' section — small overstatements that don't change the overall picture.

claims.claim: 3 blocks (element types) in the Blocks folder: richTextBlock, imageBlock (Media Picker + caption), quoteBlock (Quote + attribution)
claims.evidence: snapshot.json has the element types imageBlock, quoteBlock and richTextBlock in folder 'Blocks' with these properties

claims.claim: 1 data type: Blog Block Grid (Umbraco.BlockGrid, 12 columns, all 3 blocks configured)
claims.evidence: grade.md lists 'Blog Block Grid' in Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid, 12 columns, allowing the three blocks; check.json schema.blockGridOnPages passes

claims.claim: 2 page types in the Pages folder: blogFrontPage (title, intro, body) and blogPost (title, publishDate, excerpt, listingImage, body)
claims.evidence: snapshot.json shows both types in folder 'Pages' with exactly these property aliases

claims.claim: 2 templates assigned to their respective document types
claims.evidence: check.json counts.templates = 2; grade.md says the templates have the same names as the types

claims.claim: Allowed children: siteRoot allows blogFrontPage, blogFrontPage allows blogPost
claims.evidence: snapshot.json: blogFrontPage allowedChildren ['blogPost']; grade.md gives the tree as siteRoot → blogFrontPage → blogPost. The report does not mention that blogFrontPage is still allowedAsRoot: true (minor issue in grade.md)

claims.claim: Domain / assigned to the Blog front page
Blog front page titled 'Why MCP is Awesome' with intro and one rich text block; two posts, each with 4 blocks (rich text, image, rich text, quote)
claims.evidence: check.json crawl h1 'Why MCP is Awesome'; grade.md confirms the block structure; blogpost screenshot shows rich text → image → rich text → quote

claims.claim: 4 photos imported from unsplash/ into a 'Blog Photos' media folder
claims.evidence: check.json content.mediaFromProvidedPhotos '4 of 4 media file(s) are the provided photos' and content.mediaInFolders passes; uSync Media/blog-photos.config
check.json crawl shows 3 pages (front page + 2 posts). Minor wording slip, since the report later lists all three

claims.claim: Pages render through GetBlockGridHtmlAsync, 3 adapters, 3 ViewComponents, plain view models in Models/Blocks/
claims.evidence: check.json code.pagesUseBlockGridHelper, code.adapterPerBlock (3), code.viewComponentPerBlock (ImageBlock, QuoteBlock, RichText), and added files in Models/Blocks/*ViewModel.cs all match

claims.claim: Tailwind CSS via the Frontend project's build pipeline
claims.evidence: check.json code.frontendBuilt and site.stylesheetsLoad /dist/site.css → 200; the screenshots show a styled Tailwind layout

claims.claim: All three pages return 200 with no errors
claims.evidence: check.json crawl: all 3 paths have status 200 and empty renderErrors

claims.claim: All images display via GetCropUrl() signed URLs
claims.evidence: check.json crawl assets: 4 /media/ image URLs with hmac all return 200; site.noUnsignedResizeUrls passes

claims.claim: Block Grid renders through umb-block-grid partials (no custom render loops)
All checks pass / HTML is rendered correctly (no 'not working' section)
claims.evidence: pages/*.html line 69 renders the quote attribution as '— — …', and the blogpost screenshot shows '— — AI Developer Community, 2026'. Rich-text paragraphs also have no spacing (grade.md). These are small cosmetic flaws the model could have seen in its curl output, and the report does not mention them

claims.claim: How to view: dotnet run in Umbraco.Bench.Umbraco, visit https://localhost:44317/
claims.evidence: The site boots and serves / with 200 (check.json site.boots, site.frontPage200). The exact port is not recorded in the evidence files
